title: CALLED TO MAGNIFY THE LAW: LORD INCREASE OUR FAITH

sense.text:
“In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established”: that is the law. Being called means we are requested of God to magnify his law, and in that process we must continue to build and increase our faith. There is only one way to do that: with action and serving the Lord.

Once we begin to keep God’s commandments in the faith of Christ, the Lord starts testing us, the great fiery trial of our faith, to show us that the faith he created us with is in us. We just have to bring it out.

“Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me”: Paul was in the spirit of Christ, and he was explaining that all the things he spoke of, he was strong in Christ, strong in the power of the Lord. Christ is his source. Christ is the power.

“For we also are weak in him”: the mortal body. We all have down times, and that is why we need to increase our faith. We are not immortal yet, so Christ is here to maintain and build our faith. When we are at our weakest, that is when Christ is strong within us.

That is the key thing to remember as times get hard: we do have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. Paul understood that.

“Examine yourselves”: this is where we are right now. Look at that man in the mirror, that sister in the mirror. Measure your mind and your spirit, where you are in this faith, with the scriptures. Every one of us has a lot to work on, and we take the oversight in the spirit of humility from the gate, because we must prepare our souls for the temptation to come. The Lord does not want to lose any of us. He chose us. He did not call us by mistake, and now that we are called we must prove God to be right on the earth.

“Prove your own selves”: a lot of times we have self-doubt. Keep the commandments in the faith of Christ, knowing you are Israel, and maintain what you have learned, the things you are assured of by the bishops, the deacons, the captains and the teachers. There is a level of confidence we must build within ourselves to endure until the end.

“Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” If you cannot examine whether you are in this, ask why the Lord called you: to magnify God’s law and make it honourable. He did not call you for no reason. If you are in sin, just repent. If you are depressed, down and out, the help is not going out or only talking to a friend. It is building your spirit up in the face of these words. That is the cure.

How can you be in the truth and deny the truth, wanting to continue to be a whoremonger, a thief, a liar, deceitful? The truth is supposed to expose those things within us so we can examine ourselves and be closer to God. Sisters want to give up their whole marriages; brothers and sisters are bitter with each other at the Lord’s Passover, leaven in the body. It is not the end of the road. No temptation we go through is uncommon to man, and the Lord will give a way to escape. Without faith, we have to believe.

How do we build our faith when we are down and out, low in the spirit? The Bible gives the answer: “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” Are you reading? It sounds cliche, but study, pray, apply every single day. Pray three times a day; make it a habit. Examine whether you are within that basic instruction: are you within the scriptures?

Faith comes by hearing. The Lord said it is that simple. The way you receive the Holy Ghost is to hear what you read and what you are studying: rehearse it, bethink who you are, and believe. Faith is not only a belief system within you; it is also an action.

So faith only comes by listening, reading, studying and rehearsing the word of God, and that is the first part of the help. When you are down and out, open your Bible and read, and read according to what you are dealing with. There are classes on faith and on depression: listen, take your notes, and it will strengthen your spirit to endure. When you do not do these things, you deprive yourself of your own salvation.

precepts.why:
What is the word of God? From 2 Corinthians 13: this mortal body is weak, and without the Lord our mindset is weak. What cures that weakness and brings us into strength, endurance, that spiritual introduction to immortality? God’s word, building up our most holy faith.

Ezra speaks of them “that are cured with his word.” What cures our depression? His word. What cures our anger? His word. What cures our non-belief, and the thought that we have no purpose in life? His word.

When we compare and examine our spirit with this Bible, we find ourselves right there in Isaiah, right there in Jeremiah, going through that drunkenness, and we see how to overcome it. That should build the spirit up to endure and overcome. God is genius enough to write your history, your life, in this book, and only you are going to understand it. Being called to magnify God’s law is no damn coincidence: the Lord chose you to make sure the earth knows that God is real.

In following God’s word there comes a level of fear: you start to see what God says will happen to you if you break his commandments and stray from his laws. Like David we pray, please do not take the Holy Spirit away from me, because we have seen brothers and sisters in this truth doing well, then life came, sin started, and they got wrapped up in it until they were unrecognizable, dirty on the street, homeless, who were mighty men and women of the Lord before.

When we first came into this truth we could not put the Bible down: biblical insomnia, video after video, Bibles and highlighters stacked high. Then it got regular, and we stopped reading, studying and even praying as much. “He that keepeth the law of the Lord getteth the understanding thereof”: keeping the law is how you start to understand what God is really saying and how it pertains to you.

“And the perfection of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.” In studying the law, getting around your brothers and sisters, seeking counsel, studying and reading, you perfect your fear of the Lord. Sin does not just happen: you entertain it, you put it there, you leave it there, you make provisions for it, because there is no fear. What if the Lord does it right as you leave here, a steel rebar off a truck through your head, because you just texted the baby daddy that is still spitting game? The Lord says in Proverbs 1 he will laugh at your calamity. So stop playing with the Lord and come back.

We all struggle with something, but struggle with it; do not let it defeat you. Sinning does not mean you give up, lose rank, or exile yourself from the body. Israel United in Christ is built on the betterment of the souls of God’s people, so that you grow and get better from your sin. We cannot take this calling for granted. It is not a trend or a fashion; it is a way of life. Seek your own soul’s salvation and build your nation in righteousness. We are all in captivity.

sense.text:
“Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” These are not only your bodily eyes. These are your spiritual eyes: you have to see this word, the situation you are in, and have the insight that this is all spiritual.

We need to delve into the scriptures, meditate and read the Bible, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law. And the first wondrous thing out of God’s commandments is that he wants us to be like him. God gave the law so that we can be like unto him.

precepts.why: Christ says it, in red: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” This is the wondrous thing out of the law: when we keep God’s commandments, he wants us to be like him. Those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence, see it right there.

This is what being perfect meant in the Old Testament. Christ told Moses: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.”

God is holy, and he said ye shall be holy. Holy is us coming into perfection. That is the wondrous thing beheld out of God’s law.

sense.text:
What makes us perfect? There is one way we learn to become perfect: we must hear the word of God first.

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” That is why we are here. Some will not believe, but their unbelief does not make the faith of God of none effect. You have the sun, the moon and the stars. Go outside the firmament and you cannot breathe. Who made all of that? How does the sun stay ablaze, burning so hot so permanently, where there is no oxygen? There must be a God. Not one negro, not one damn Egyptologist can make a star, let alone reach it, but they want to worship it.

With all this, you know God is real. How much more should you show him in your conversation and in your actions, by not sinning? That is really the point.

“There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” The word of God is preached in all languages of the earth. From the beginning in Genesis, when the languages were confused, God’s laws were not negated. In Acts 2 they spoke the languages of the lands, and God’s laws stayed the same. Thou shalt not kill means the same thing in China, Russia, Malaysia, the Solomon Islands, in Malawi in Chichewa, and in Portuguese where some of our people speak it. God’s laws are magnified in all places.

The spirit of the Lord opened our ears to go out and preach his gospel throughout the whole planet earth. That is where we are in history: fulfilling what we read in the scriptures. So how much more should you see yourself in this Bible, knowing you are Israel? Do not lose your faith; strengthen and increase it, because times are getting harder. There will come a time when you will not be worried about any damn job, only praying, Lord, help me make it to the next new moon.
“Their line is gone out through all the earth”: our line, our lineage, our legacy, your reputation, your teaching, the works you put in for this gospel’s sake, going “to the end of the world.”

“As a bridegroom coming out of his chamber”: the bridegroom is Christ. When the scriptures say, well done, my good and faithful servant, it is the bridegroom proud of the one he made for a tabernacle that the sun can light up. You are a vessel made for honour. You are the gold, because you fulfilled the purpose you were created for.

“The law of the Lord is perfect.” Why are the laws of the Lord perfect? Because God’s laws are his ways, his habits, and he gave them unto his children.

“Converting the soul”: converting us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for salvation and the redemption of our souls.

“Making wise the simple.” We were simple; some called themselves X. Then we converted, striving now for perfection, and came back to the understanding that we are Israel, the Israelites. That is the converting of our souls. For so long, through slavery and oppression, we lost our way. Now we must come to the point of bethinking ourselves.

In oppression the Lord opens our understanding, our minds, our ears, and makes our eyes see his law. After we understand and observe, we have to apply it and be like our Father.

“He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.” Two questions follow: who are the poor, and how have we become poor?

You only understand who you are in times of hardship. The Lord proves you are worthy when the pressure is put on you. Pressure bursts pipes; diamonds are made under pressure; gold is tried in the fire. You cannot come to perfection without trials and tribulations, and enduring them: the relationship problems, the unbelieving spouse, the unbelieving child, the unbelieving family members. Will you give up the unbelieving and wicked that make it hard to keep this faith, for the sake of Christ? Compare salvation to giving up a carnal job and there is no comparison. That career is not worth your soul.

“He openeth also their ear to discipline”: when you realized, wait, the way I show I love God is to keep his commandments, and you subdued your understanding. The discipline is the Holy Spirit of discipline: his laws, statutes and commandments. He opened your ears and showed you were doing it the wrong way.

People say they hate camps, but camps are the only reason you understand the Bible the way you do. The white man did not tell you that you are an Israelite. God put the spirit on the men that came before us and those that followed, the elders like Elder Marshall, and we got the fruits of that in our bishops today. The spirit of Elijah continued among us: we bethought ourselves, were brought back to our fathers, and the history was brought back to us. That is prophecy. And those that hate God’s people use our own people to try to destroy it, betraying their own people to appease the red hair of the enemy, Edom.

“And commandeth that they return from iniquity”: commanded, requested, called, that you return from iniquity back to your heritage.

“He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.” The oppression is the oppressor and the religion he gave us. Esau is not poor; he is rich through robbery, and that continues to this day. We were robbed and spoiled and hid in prison houses, as Isaiah 42:22 says.

Just because you are not in the prison system does not mean you are not in captivity. Deuteronomy 28 applies to us: the Lord gave the warning, we did not take heed, and the curses are in full effect. The 13th Amendment ended slavery except as punishment for crime, and that loophole filled the prisons with our people as free labor for the corporations. The illusion of democracy gave the feeling that slavery was abolished, but slavery has only evolved. In Egypt they dealt craftily with us; it is the same today. This is still the land of our captivity; it never changed, your enemy just got crafty with you. Like Neo in the fourth Matrix, the system upgraded until he forgot he was ever free, and his whole life was assimilated while in his mind he was still in oppression.

We are not supposed to be at rest in this land. When you lose and lack that faith, you lose sight of your purpose in life. It is not to be a damn slave or a negro. Your nine to five is for you to keep these commandments, to remember that you are called and requested of God, and to magnify his law upon the earth. Watch and pray, and see yourself outside this system, preparing your mind for the return of the true Messiah; the deceptions will be so strong that if it were possible they would deceive the very elect.

precepts.why:
We are here to prove who the poor are. Nobody can praise and serve the Lord like the poor. “Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith”: why are we rich in faith? Because God chose you. He called you; he requested you. Now we must continue to endure and increase our faith, not only in hard times but in dealing with one another: in our families, in marriage.

In the time of our oppression, faith is the only thing that will keep us together, and you are not alone: your brother, your sister, your nation keeping the Sabbath with you builds your faith. Going to various places on the planet and seeing our people understand this word fulfills the prophecies of God, and that should build your faith. Trust not in man, but in the process: God’s prophecies being fulfilled through the men he inspired to preach this gospel.

“And heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him.” Them that love him keep his commandments, and they show it with their faith, preparing their minds for the return of our Messiah, the black Messiah, Christ, whom we preach and confess throughout the whole world.

sense.text:
The meaning of this class is to increase our faith in the Most High God in the spirit of Christ, to remember who we are, bethink ourselves, and encourage endurance in righteousness. For righteousness’ sake we must endure hard times, because hard times bring us to perfection. It is also to teach us to stand against sin, deception and spiritual wickedness in high places. It is not only physical; it is mental, a battle fatigue where you lose your confidence. Coming into this faith is not the end of the road; you have not made it. Without faith it is impossible to please God.

How did we become poor? “But this is a people robbed and spoiled.” We were robbed of our land and our nationality, our culture, our heritage, our riches, wealth, resources and economics. In Malawi they say David Livingstone brought civilization, but before that they had wealth and economics. When we came from Jerusalem down into Africa and scattered throughout the world, we had all of that, and we were robbed of everything. Then we were spoiled: that word means destroyed. We were destroyed for the lack of knowledge and given a false heritage, destroyed with the religions of our oppressor. How can your oppressor be your God? It makes no sense.

The brothers in Papua New Guinea are not the heathen; they are of the tribe of Naphtali. The Lord said we would be scattered to the four corners of the earth.

Our ancestors in slavery had much faith; that is why we are here. Some understood the Bible even in a polluted sense, like Nat Turner. With the gifts of sports, entertainment and jobs, given to make us feel assimilated and included, our strength toward our God was weakened and we forgot him.

Right now a brother or sister is second-guessing whether to stay in this truth. Last night the phone rang, we going out; before you were strong enough to say I do not do that no more, but last night you thought about it twice. Next week you put the clothes on; the week after, I will go but I am not staying long. That is a setup, and that is going back to your vomit. Your ex DMs, what are you doing, and you answer, nothing. That is the battle, the devil of your baby mama, your baby daddy. That is why Paul asked, Lord, take this away, and the Lord said no: it keeps you humble, and there is no glory if everything is just taken away. You must be tried in that fire and say no. Possession is a series of yeses: from the first time you said yes to stealing, you gave place to the devil.

“They are all of them snared in holes, and they are hid in prison houses”: it still takes effect to this day. We were robbed of our land, our nationality and who we are, and then given a false identity, and we think that is our faith.

precepts.why:
When we were robbed and spoiled, we were given another god and another identity. We stopped putting our faith in the one true God, and we forgot.

“O Lord our God”: the same God that made the heavens by his workmanship, by his hands. People worship the sun, the moon and the stars; we have a God that created all of that. The God of our ancestors is not the God of all people, thus saith the Bible. That is why it sounds uncommon to your ears: this Bible has been preached to you by your oppressor, by Esau, Edom, by Cesare Borgia, by presidents you treat as God. The Bible says they are the wicked that God has given the earth unto.

“Other lords beside thee have had dominion over us.” The Lord gave a prime example with the Egyptians, how he destroyed them, and he will continue to destroy all those whom God’s people think are gods and are not the one true God. When we put our trust in our oppressor, we make an agreement with hell, with death.

“But by thee only will we make mention of thy name”: by the one true God that called us to understand his word plainly, the servants he gave the secret of his word to. Coming into this word is not the end goal; it is the beginning of our trial. God did not call you for no damn reason. It is not a coincidence that you understand and hear this word.

sense.text:
Who are the poor? “That the Lord hath founded Zion”: Zion is the city of David in Israel, the twelve tribes of Israel, Judah, Benjamin, Levi and the rest.

“And the poor of his people”: God’s people. We became poor through the various captivities: our identity, that seed, polluted through indoctrination among the nations, and we were robbed of who we are, spoiled and destroyed.

But the spirit remains the same. That is why within our nation we have many shades, light and dark: the seed of Israel mingled among the nations, but the spirit God chose to be his people still remains in us. That is why we go to all the nations and teach our people in those lands. We are there, because of our sins and our oppression.

“Shall trust in it”: we shall trust in our Lord, not the ways of the nations or of this world.

precepts.why:
This is the good news we trust in. We have been made poor, humbled, destroyed and cut off, yet in 2026 we know we are the Israelites, we know Christ is black, and we have blitzed the entire planet earth with the word of God. The gates of hell cannot prevail.

“And fear not, my son, that we are made poor: for thou hast much wealth.” We have much wealth, because everything pertaining to the Bible, the glory, the riches, the kingdom, belongs to us.

What is the stipulation? “If thou fear God, and depart from all sin, and do that which is pleasing in his sight.” Whatever trials of faith you are going through, God said you are wealthy if you fear him and depart from your sin. Keep the commandments and you will get the kingdom. No matter what these nations have done to bring us to a lower state, fear God and keep his commandments.

sense.text:
“I will liken my judgment unto a ring.” God shall be known in his judgments. As Deuteronomy says, when we sin we find ourselves back in captivity, slavery and the prison houses, and his judgment stands. It is sure; his prophecies are fulfilled.

That is what we are showing: God is here. So take heed and fear God according to the scriptures.

There was a clause; read the fine print. Slavery is abolished, except if you are in jail or prison. Why do they fill up the prison houses? Slavery. They have the power to go to the moon and the satellites to watch everything, but they cannot stop the drugs and guns in the community? They do not want to. The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. We have to obey the laws of God, and the laws of the land, so we do not get caught up in the oppression.

It is the man of sin, the white man, the devil the Bible speaks of. Go to Japan or China and there is virtually zero crime; in Dubai you can leave your Bugatti outside with the doors open and nobody will steal it. Not that they are righteous: the Lord is going to destroy all of them. But wherever the white man is, wherever Esau is, England or here, it is rampant with theft, robbery, drugs and prostitution, and America, the so-called greatest country on earth, imprisons more people than every other country combined.

“Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee?” No. Christ, God and the angels are black, and the throne of iniquity has nothing to do with Christmas, Valentine’s Day, or the false man-made religions made by your oppressor. The president is not God and does not serve the one true God. Armageddon will come.

“Which frameth mischief by a law”: they framed deceit and mischief, misled us with democracy and freedom, and made it law. An amendment is like a commandment, the statutes of their societal government: slavery is abolished, but if you are in a system of crime you go back to slavery. Some people do need to be locked up if they rob and steal; that is why other nations police our communities. What we institute is the keeping of God’s commandments, so you stay far from that.

A young man facing the death penalty, and the former warden says the prison would benefit from him: he is young, he is healthy, we need that labor, that sweat equity, and we will put him out there to work. Sweat equity is slavery. The plea is, do not kill him, make him a slave, for free labor at the sweatshops of McDonald’s and Victoria’s Secret, paid next to nothing while they make billions off your black back. It is the Willie Lynch letter: beat him within an inch of his life, but do not kill him, because it is not good for economics. He is twenty and has sixty, seventy years of labor in him, making big rocks into little rocks. That is evil as hell.

This world is filled with confusion, false religion, violence, immorality, deceit with artificial intelligence, a false Messiah, hatred of the righteous, women out of order, men that will not step up and guide their households in a godly fashion. We are an organized moral nation built on God’s commandments, and clarifying these things increases our faith.

“Who is blind, but my servant? or deaf, as my messenger that I sent?” Israel doth not consider. We do not even know that we are Israel: the ox knows his owner and the ass his master’s crib, but Israel doth not know. We did not consider that we ourselves are the servants, that we must come to perfection, that we are the messengers, the children of God.

At one point we were blind, but now we see. We were deaf, but now we hear discipline: the Lord opened our ears so we can understand his word and fulfill our destiny, our vocation. That is why you are here, brother, sister, children: to be raised in the ways of the Lord and magnify his law.

“The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake”: for his holiness, his commandments, his ways. Even though we were deaf and blind, he is pleased when you are just like him, when your ears are open to his discipline: that is my boy, that is my girl, in whom I am well pleased.

“He will magnify the law, and make it honourable.” If the Lord came down right now we would all be dead; we could not take it in the wilderness. He will magnify the law through Christ and make it honourable, and Christ said greater things than these shall you do. So we continue in that process of magnifying the law through Christ and making his word honourable on the planet.

Marriage is an honourable thing, and that is why Satan had to attack it. Brotherhood, unity, nationhood, raising your children, not stealing, not killing, loving your nation as you love yourself: that is a superpower, a weapon. Our love, our nation and keeping God’s commandments is the power, and that is what they try to destroy.

“If they sin against thee, (for there is no man which sinneth not,)” and the Lord delivers them to their enemies, and “they carry them away captives unto a land far off or near”: far off means scattered throughout the nations; near means close to Jerusalem, the homeland.

“Yet if they bethink themselves in the land whither they are carried captive”: in the land of our captivity, scattered far or near, if Israel bethinks itself. To bethink is to remember or recall: to cause oneself to be reminded, or to cause oneself to consider. That is why the law says remember: remember the Sabbath day, remember your heritage, that God created the earth in six days and rested on the seventh and made the Sabbath a sign between him and the children of Israel. The Sabbath is vital to our salvation, our growth and understanding our true heritage.

How do we bethink ourselves? By hearing the word of God and understanding it. When you can explain this word, and see it fulfilled in real time, the tribulation, the hard times, many deceived, being afflicted for righteousness’ sake, it should build your faith. When hard times come, it should increase your faith. Pray for hard times, and pray that God increases your faith. When you go to other countries and see their hardships, what is this life about? Being comfortable? No. We must stop trusting in the love of our oppressors and come into the position of being delivered out of Egypt.

“Saying, We have sinned, we have done amiss, and have dealt wickedly”: done amiss from the laws. In captivity we must learn to suffer and be delivered with righteousness: keep God’s commandments while under oppression. You say you are not oppressed, you have no chains, but you clock in nine to five, and as soon as you do things for your nation you go right back to clocking in. That spirit of working dims the flame: rest, eat, back to work. Build your faith up and understand this is not our rest.

precepts.why:
How do we faint? When we bethink ourselves, we remember in captivity the suffering we suffered, and we come out of that oppression by keeping God’s commandments. Christ said you shall know the truth and the truth shall make you free: from your sin, from mental slavery and from actual enslavement. We are saved and delivered when we endure.

“Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net.” What people on the planet are at the head of every street corner? That is us. They ignorantly call us YNs, and we call ourselves YNs: uncs and OGs and all this BS. That is not your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings? We fainted, we are hid in prison houses and on every corner: on 18th Street, in the Pork and Beans projects in Miami, in the Bronx, in every hood and ghetto in the earth, our people.

When we bethink ourselves, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are. “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”: prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors.

When you learn from the examples of our ancestors, it gives a guide to how we need to be today. That is legacy. How did our ancestors handle famine, persecution and tribulation? They dialed into the scriptures.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”: the things our fathers went through are written for our learning, to increase our faith. It is no longer, I am a YN; we have young prophets among us. We are raising our sons and daughters, young men, teens, young adults, in the understanding that they are the children of the prophets, the sons and daughters of God.

“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” That spirit of comfort, when you hear the word and the hairs on your skin rise, is the spirit of Christ, confirmation that you are in this. It is a pride, not in an evil way, but appreciation, dignity and integrity of who you are.

The scriptures give you hope to endure the times we are in, that we might tap into the faith we should be building ourselves up on.

sense.text:
These are the steps for increasing our faith, by example of Job. We are called, we understand we are Israel because of the curses, and we see what is going on in the world through the scriptures. Then comes the question: what do I do? We have to build and increase our faith, and Job shows the mindset in a hard and trying time.

“Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Job said the Lord gave and he can take away, and he did not blaspheme. He was righteous in his understanding, and that is how we have to be.

“In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.” Job lost his children, he lost his wealth, he had boils and sicknesses, and he endured all of it to glorify and magnify the Lord. Job was called to prove that God is real, and the Lord proved to Satan and the world, that is my servant.

precepts.why:
How did Job do it? The mindset: evil is going to come our way, so embrace it. Pray for hard times, because our people only turn to God when things go crazy: when you lose your job, when a death happens, when you are treated wrong. When you are low, depressed and oppressed, you have an outlet, a sanctuary, a home, and those who can lead you to it. With the faith of Christ, our heavenly Father and keeping God’s commandments, we are going to need each other.

“And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also.” Praying for hard times is also praying for the destruction of our enemies, and preparing ourselves for temptation. Embrace that this mission is not for us to be comfortable, and you can build your spirit up to handle hard times. When the virus came and the whole earth stopped, what grounded us, our anchor, was God’s word, still keeping the Sabbath. Many went back into the world. It will get worse. Thank the Lord for hard times: they make you pure as gold; the pressure makes you a diamond, a ruby. Like tears in a muscle, the hardship makes your spiritual muscles stronger. But you only get there by hearing the word of God, studying and preparing your mind.

“Knowing that tribulation worketh patience”: knowing. Prepare for the worst and hope for the best. The deacons, the bishops and the captains have been preparing us: famine, death, judgment like a wheel. Prepare in your household. Some do not have a bag of rice in a Mylar bag or a system for water. We have a prepping team; take it seriously. Preserving and keeping storehouses is part of our heritage.

“And patience, experience”: not only the food, the famine and the water, but the sword and war when they persecute us. Job went through it personally; as a nation with families, children and wives, we must increase our faith and prepare together, because those labor pains are coming back around like a judgment.

“And experience, hope”: having experienced the tribulations, we build our hope, our faith. “And hope maketh not ashamed”: I am not ashamed, because my Lord will comfort me, and in hard times I have brother and sister, family, order and structure in my household and our nation. That comfort keeps us on track, enduring until the end.

sense.text: We are back again doing the same thing we did before, regeneration: we are who the Lord called us to be. “And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost”: the Holy Spirit of discipline.

“They had all things common.” At the blitz in Orlando, Captain Ship said we have to stop living beyond our means and be content with our wages and in life. A family of seven may need a house with some room, but a single brother buying a mansion and expensive cars, do you know the times we are living in?

Live below your means. A time is coming when you will not be worried about gas prices or maintaining your BMW or Bugatti. We are not rich. Money, riches, comfort and wealth should not be your god, keeping up with the Joneses and the American dream that is a lie. We have to have all things in common, in faith and understanding, so that we do not lose and sell out our souls.

“Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them”: that is the point. Live below your means, not beyond.

“And distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.” This nation is big, and millions of our people lack. When you sacrifice your much, it is much to them that have little. To experience that, we must travel, go and spread this gospel abroad.

precepts.why:
We live in an era where vanity is a drug and attention is a drug. At the Rolling Loud blitz, kids said they want to be streamers. That is what is common now. What about a plumber, a mechanic, a builder, an architect, a lawyer, an engineer, the things that build nations? That is why we have been destroyed as a people. We are destroyed, but we are getting healed.

“Some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits”: because of money, wealth and the many things that distract us from God, from Christ and from our purpose in life. “And doctrines of devils”: religion, man-made religion.

“Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: politics is a lie, to make you feel assimilated in a government that is kicking you out of it. One black governor in this whole country; the black generals removed as not qualified; making their country great again in their eyes. We have been streaming us repenting as a people, and men and women in the faith want to leave it to stream in the world.

“Having their conscience seared with a hot iron”: by religion, politics and the gifts of this world. “Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received”

“In the last days perilous times shall come.” In perilous times we have to have all things in common and build our faith.

“For men shall be lovers of their own selves”: going for likes, not worried about being an aid to your society and community. Me, me, me: how many likes and followers? It is not about you; it is about your people.

“Covetous, boasters”: boasting of vanity, money, drugs, houses, cars, women. “Proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful”: not appreciative of God and what he has done for you. “Unholy”: this is the nature of them that go after the world and the gift that destroys the heart. “Without natural affection.”

sense.text:
What steps did our ancestors take to maintain the integrity of their faith? How can we talk about faith without understanding what faith is?

“Now faith is the substance of things hoped for”: you hear the word and believe it will come to pass. It is a thought, a feeling, a belief system first, and first for a reason. “The evidence of things not seen.”

In the Christianity we were taught, the thinking is where it stops. They do not understand what faith truly is. Faith is proven through action: faith without works is dead.

“For by it the elders obtained a good report.” A report is action, a reputation of doing something. It was not just that Abraham, Sarah, Job, David and Aaron believed and so got through. There were actions behind the faith they had.

“By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place”: Abraham was called, requested of God to go out. He was a sojourner, in a sense homeless, until he came to a land where he could facilitate living. He had wealth, camels and everything, but no roof over his head.

“Obeyed”: obedience is an action. “And he went out, not knowing whither he went”: he trusted the Lord, who told him, get thee out of the land of your nativity, and go.

“Dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob”: tents, as was common in our culture. If we miss one night in our house, we begin to lose faith; Abraham our father showed integrity through the hard times. We are going to have to get back to dwelling in booths, tabernacles or caves with our children, our wives and our families. Who else did it but us? We are them; they are us.

“For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.” The things written aforetime are written for our learning. We need to prepare to be able to sojourn, not in our comfort: bug-in and bug-out bags, a plan for when things pop off, having these conversations with your children and building them up now, not at some certain age, and building up your wife, so that without amazement she is not confused or afraid.

“Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed.” Sarah is brought out with Abraham because, after dealing with the individual, Job, in tribulation, the faith of the marriage, man and woman together, must be built up for hard times.

Peter gave the instructions between marriages for how to endure tribulation and receive blessing from God. We have marriage counsels where a sister is upset because the socks are on the floor and calls her husband lazy, or a sister gives up the faith to go back to the world and be a hoe to negro Tyrone instead of a wife to the husband the Lord gave her, or a brother wants to be a whoremonger instead of a man leading his people. More trying times are coming, when you will be worried about surviving. How much more must a household where man and woman are striving with each other get right?

“But and if ye suffer for righteousness’ sake”: we must learn to suffer for the sake of Christ and righteousness. “Happy are ye”: that is your peace. Happy are they that keep God’s laws. Prepare for hard and trying times, and do not go railing for railing with one another. Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying and increasing our faith, and following the instructions laid forth.

“And be not afraid of their terror”: not afraid of being persecuted. For the sake of righteousness we went through hell on earth, yet we had happiness and peace, because the poor of God’s people were rich in faith. This is in a sense the easiest time of our generation, because we are so destroyed we do not even know who we are; before this were Jim Crow and the black codes, when the black church was actually doing something for the community, and before that slavery, and before that the hell of sin. So we learn what is going to happen to us from what happened to us before.

precepts.why: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” Nothing shall offend them: being afraid of tribulation will not offend you so that you turn your back on Christ. That is the happiness of them that suffer for righteousness’ sake.

sense.text:
A time in our ancestry when we were persecuted and endured. “In those days went there out of Israel wicked men”: out of our own people come forth the wicked of our nation. Under terror and tribulation our people are controlled by our oppressors, and they use our own people to destroy and oppress us. It comes from your enemy.

“Who persuaded many”: persuaded them back into sin. “Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen”: today we make that covenant when we facilitate ourselves in their politics, their religion, their government, the gifts that destroy the heart. And the women of our people were there too, turning our people back to evil.

“For since we departed from them we have had much sorrow”: the same thing said in Egypt, let us go back to the melons and the cucumbers and the leeks; Egypt took care of us. A black pastor praying over a golden statue of the president is a prime example: wicked of our own people making the covenant. The first commandment says no other gods and no graven image, but that is his god, an agreement with Satan, an agreement with hell. We bring it up so you know what not to do: do not be deceived by the worship of the gods of Babylon, who make themselves God.

“They went to the king, who gave them licence to do after the ordinances of the heathen”: they asked to be part of their government and system, to be assimilated, to call themselves Antiochians; in this day, I want to be an American. We assimilated because we were robbed and spoiled of our nation and heritage and became poor, so we grope at noonday like the blind toward whatever we think will bring comfort, and forget our one true God.
“According to the customs of the heathen”: we began to be like them.

precepts.why:
What did God say? “Envy thou not the oppressor”: do not be jealous of the oppressor or want to emulate him. “And choose none of his ways”: his religion, his way of thinking, his economics, his way of life. Bethink how we need to be, and use this world without abusing it and losing your soul.

“For the froward is abomination to the Lord”: to go forward in sin in that direction is an abomination to God. “But his secret is with the righteous.”

sense.text:
The pride in the mind of all oppressors is so high they make themselves as God. Christ is not white, not Caucasian, not red, not an Edomite; the Bible explains plainly that Christ is black. That is common knowledge to you, but elsewhere in the earth they are deceived with Cesare Borgia, the Pope’s son.

“And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies.” A show where Christ gives the crown of thorns to a fictitious superhero meant to be the savior of America is a form of blasphemy, coming out while they say make America great again and push us back into servitude, where in their eyes we know our place. It is predictive programming, preparing you until it is the norm and you are desensitized.

But there is a safe haven: Israel United in Christ, and those throughout the world keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ. We are decoding ourselves out of that system and the lie they tried to force on us. Continue your faith, build on it, and endure.

precepts.why:
Their pride has reached to the heights of heaven: I will call myself Jesus and force you to think it, set myself up as the savior of countries, put myself in a golden statue, while saying I am not even a Christian. These are not your gods, family; do not lose sight of the one true God.

“So they shall make their own tongue to fall upon themselves: all that see them shall flee away.” The information comes out from their own whistleblowers, and they say, what are you going to do about it? In their eyes neither you nor God can stop it, but there will be a reckoning.

This is what 1 Maccabees said: the wicked of our own people make a covenant, a black pastor praying over the statue, our people gravitating toward these things. The show is a similitude of what is happening in real time.

“He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.” All praises to the Most High, the Lord dismantled one of those arms of persecution, the SPLC, caught up in their own BS. Whoever gets credit, they are all the same, and they will raise another organization to come against us, though all we do is promote marriage and the righteous family, man and woman, like Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Joseph and Mary.

sense.text:
In hard times Satan attacks the marriage. He did not attack the government Adam set up first; he attacked the foundation, the marriage, which shows how powerful marriage is. He went through the woman first, which is why sisters have to build themselves up. Marriage is honourable and the bed undefiled.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives.” Sisters, your tone and how you speak to your husband, especially in hard times, means a lot. How you respect your lord, your king in your household, how you project yourself toward him, shows the level of your faith. Increase your faith and learn to be correct with the man God gave you. And not only wives: all you sisters must honour the men of your nation.

The first step in building up your faith: read and search the scriptures. We use these examples to warn us today what not to do. Prepare your soul for the search of your fathers; in your patience possess ye your soul. When you see yourself in the scriptures, that is the solution, the cure to how you are processing. We have to go through these things to prove God is real on the earth, and when you see the prophecies fulfilled, your faith should increase even the more.

“Search the scriptures.” When we see the tribulations come to pass, captivity and chains, persecution for his righteousness’ sake, the wicked of our people assimilating with the enemy, we should say, wait, this is in the scriptures.

“For in them ye think ye have eternal life”: the other side of it is the salvation written for us, when we all become righteous and are not deceived by the things of this world. Faith begins with knowledge, understanding and study. You cannot really believe in something you do not know, so we make it a habit to continue to study.

precepts.why:
“Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law”: open our eyes, our minds and our understanding. This Bible is the book of the laws of God. Moses gave the law, and the prophets spoke of our reputation: what happened when we broke God’s laws, and the mercy we received when we came back to them and kept the commandments.

“I am a stranger in the earth.”

sense.text:
The second step: once you build yourself up, you separate yourself from evil.

“Return unto the Lord”: repent, remember, bethink. “And forsake thy sins”: you come in, learn what to do and what not to do.

“Make thy prayer before his face.” Why does it mention his face? Because of our sins he turned himself from us. When you repent and return in your actions, you seek him early and acknowledge your sin. His face, and what he looks like, matters, because we have been praying to the wrong God from the beginning. Since we got off those ships, our oppressors made themselves our God and had dominion over us. So we subdue our understanding and separate ourselves from evil, the ways of our oppressor.

“And offend less”: be ye perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect. We are striving for perfection. Offend less means stop the sin.

precepts.why:
Hate sin. “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.” “Ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards”: do not be comfortable, family. That is what Amos is saying.

“Hate the evil.” David said, I love your commandments and I hate every false way. We hate anything outside of keeping God’s commandments. We are supposed to hate sin, hate that there is sin in our community, and do something about it by keeping God’s law. We are not to tolerate evil among our people.

“And love the good”: love God’s commandments. That is your purpose; that increases your faith; that is why you are called and requested to magnify God’s law. “And establish judgment”: action, in yourself, your household, your nation and your communities. “It may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph”: you receive mercy when you hate the evil and love the good.

Separate from evil, because America blurs the line of what evil is, and that is the problem with religion and worshipping him. Your president said, what do you have to lose? Your communities are damaged, you have no education, so choose me.

“Come out of her, my people.” What are we coming out of? The evil promoted today: adultery, the music, murder, sodomy, homosexuality, drunkenness, drug abuse, idolatry, wicked entertainment and corruption, all that God hates. We must expose this evil so you can learn to save your own souls: our young people smoking weed and toting guns, women toting guns bigger than them, little kids with bullets taller than they are. Then they call us a hate group when we are trying to stop the evil in our community first.

“That ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” Sin is deceitful, and America has blurred the line.

They have made good evil and evil good. Separating yourself is the second step: study, pray, apply, see yourself in the scriptures, then show your faith by separating yourself from evil.

“Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil”: destruction unto them. “That put darkness for light, and light for darkness”: they blur the line between good and evil. Who does that? Your pastor. Many a black church is on every corner, and they facilitate the continuance of your oppression.

sense.text:
Why are we here? What is our purpose? You have to choose a side: righteousness, your heritage, your nation keeping God’s commandments, gathering together in the laws of the Most High God.

“To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light”: not your bodily eyes, because with our bodily eyes and ears we sin. Pray that in times of tribulation the Lord opens your spiritual eyes and spiritual ears, so you can see and hear his understanding, maintain your godly discipline and endure to the end.

“And from the power of Satan unto God”: we keep the commandments and the faith of Christ to encourage our people to turn from Satan to God according to the scripture. “That they may receive forgiveness of sins.” When the SPLC, the Canary Mission, AIPAC, the FBI and the CIA come against us, they do not want you to come to repentance and salvation, and they call it a cult. The people will prove who is of God, and it cannot be stopped. Christianity is losing; it is finished.

This should increase your faith. It took a lot to get here, but every flyer passed out, by a brother, a sister, a child, a young man of valor, is fulfilling prophecy, the next generation. They will esteem us as evil, but God knows we are set to do good for the world and the nation. World peace will not come until we are in rulership: the people mourn when the wicked are in authority and rejoice when the Israelites, black man, woman and child, are in position, when Christ returns.

“He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise”: what they plan in secret chambers and think tanks.

“He taketh the wise in their own craftiness”: the whistleblowers; their tongue falls upon themselves. “And the counsel of the froward is carried headlong”: the counsel of the sinful, the wicked, comes to an end. It will be finished.

“But he saveth the poor from the sword”: there is the poor again. He saves us from the sword, from destruction. “So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.” This is what we have faith in: though the times get hard, we will have deliverance and peace in those trying times, if we endure and continue in this faith.

“Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.” In this tribulation we must endure temptation and prepare ourselves. Correction builds up your faith for hard times. Losing a job, finances, people in your life are hard, but nothing is more pure and rewarding than being corrected for the sins you have done before the Lord, and continuing to endure and perfect your soul.

Nothing is more important than getting yourself right. Whatever you are going through, at least you are preparing and building up your soul and getting yourself perfect for the Most High God, for his salvation, for the true Messiah to return.

“And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly”: the Lord sanctified us when he called us. We are secure; we are comforted.

“Your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Before the return of the Lord we are commanded to preserve our souls blameless, and blameless means perfection: that we maintain our spirit with our faith and endure, so we come to perfection.

Why do we have camps and schools, places of learning? Because we always had them. The school of the prophets: Samuel was what you would call a professor, and the sons of the prophets were a system set up to raise up the teachers of Israel. Then there was the apostles’ doctrine, and those called Christians. There have always been groups of believers in Christ.

“And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets”: when Christ ascended and left, he set leadership in order, and for a purpose. Where is this order found? In what God prophesied of as a sanctuary: what we commonly call camps, schools, bodies of believers, having all things in common to gather a nation scattered abroad.

“For the perfecting of the saints”: he set up order for the perfecting of the saints. Never let anybody tell you that you cannot join Israel United in Christ because of XYZ. Boil it down and it is personal BS: nine times out of ten, really every time, there was something they did not want to get right with God. We do not profess to be perfect; we have issues, but when in error we get it together. We are back to learn Christ and the riches of the Lord’s mercies, striving for perfection. All we teach is repentance in the faith of Christ, so a problem with the body of believers is a problem with your own salvation and repentance.

Remember 1 Maccabees 1:11: wicked men went out to assimilate us and keep us from salvation. Coming out of Egypt there were Dathan and his like trying to send us back, hindering the deliverance; that is why prophets and leaders were set up. It is the same spirit today.

“For the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ.”

“Till we all come in the unity of the faith”: in Jesus Christ. That is why we are here, and why we must continue to endure.

We increase our faith so that we are not unequally yoked with this world and unbelievers; so we can heal toxic marriages and relationships, because marriage is honourable, and nurture them with fortitude in hard times instead of falling apart over money or keeping up with the Joneses. We are growing up in these schools of the prophets of the Lord to discourage sinful environments, encourage righteousness in our nation, do away with corrupt doctrines and religions and the worldly influence that weakens your faith, and come back to our heritage, our people, our God and our King.

The third step: learn to channel the sin and the pain we have suffered into righteousness. First, study, pray, apply; then turn from sin; now turn all this evil and mischief into righteousness, from the power of Satan to God, from darkness unto light, for repentance.

“Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil”: what we read before. “Cleave to that which is good.” Come home, family.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love”: looking out for each other. “In honour preferring one another.” The Lord wants our spirit right for the kingdom: honour one another in our marriages, our relationships and our nation.

“Not slothful in business.” What is our business? We are called by God and here to magnify the law and increase our faith. “Fervent in spirit; serving the Lord”: by doing the work, helping your people.
“Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer”: these are the steps. “Distributing to the necessity of saints.” What better life to live than to help your people?

“Be not overcome of evil”: do not let this world destroy your faith. “But overcome evil with good”: with the good of these commandments and the faith of Christ, knowing who you are, you overcome that evil with the good of this Bible.
